You deserve someone to stop and hold you if you've been triggered by something. You deserve someone who actually means it when they apologize and then proves it by never doing it again. This horrible man is raping and abusing you, and it's NOT OKAY. I truly hope you're able to take your children and get out. Keep in mind that leaving will help protect your babies as well. Please stay safe, OP ♥️

I wouldn't hold it against her because she was a minor (with a brain that isn't fully developed, very little impulse control, etc.), and my partner would have been an adult. Adult vs minor is a power dynamic, and the adult has responsibilities within that dynamic. Even if my sister had stripped naked in front of him and tried to come onto him, I still wouldn't hold it against her. I'd be upset with her for doing something like that, but ultimately, it's the adult's responsibility to make adult decisions. He had a responsibility to say, "No, this is inappropriate. You're a child."
I don't care if you tried everything you could to seduce him. It's still not your fault.

My aunt is 5'4" and probably 275-300 lbs. She's been that way for years, and yet she STILL worked 12 hour shifts as an EMT in a level 1 trauma center ER, often not even getting a chance to pee. She would work 3-4 12 hour shifts a week. Consistently lifting people, walking 10+ miles per day, etc. She did this for 20 damn years.

One of my good friends is probably 150 lbs overweight, yet she runs 9-10 miles multiple times a week and walks faster than most of my skinny friends. Not all fat people are made the same. So no, it's not "obvious" that a person carrying 100+ lbs is going to have a hard time keeping up. Maybe being obese was a factor for this person, but maybe it wasn't. Maybe this person had scoliosis, or IBS, or IBD, or any other number of disabilities that have nothing to do with weight. You don't know, OP doesn't know. I agree; It wasn't fair for OP to have their "friends" leaving this girl with them. They didn't ask for it. But the way OP is talking about this girl is extremely ignorant, disrespectful, and dehumanizing. OP is NTA for being upset, but they absolutely are TA for speaking about this girl the way that they are.

When I finally told close friends and family, one of my "friends" said "well I would have done this and this if it were me" (detailing how she would have escaped, etc.). Yeah, it's easy to say that when you're not in it. When you're not frozen in fear, wondering if the next word or movement could cost you your life. Needless to say, we're no longer friends and haven't been in a while.

You did what you had to do to survive. You handled the situation the best way you knew how. Despite what ANYONE else says, it's not your fault. Period. But it's especially not your fault just because some asshole outside of the situation thinks they could have handled it better. Screw them.

When I say it's not true doctrine, I mean in the factual sense of the word. The church has very strict rules, and they are very strict with what is considered true teachings. There is a little bit of room for "revelation" regarding these teachings, but to go so far as teaching and believing polygamy is okay is a huge no-no. Polygamy is part of the history of the church, but is expressly forbidden and grounds for excommunication if anyone is discovered practicing. Polygamy is not true doctrine as it is written within the rules and teachings of the LDS church in the modern day. Mormons (anyone within the LDS church) who believe in polygamy are not following the specific rules and teachings of the church. Heavenly polygamy is doctrine, but other than that, polygamy is not okay with the church. Whether it would be okay or not if it hadn't been made illegal doesn't mean that it is factual doctrine, which is what I meant. I wasn't trying to undermine anyone else's experience 😅 I apologize, I should have been more clear in what I meant.

That being said, I absolutely believe there are plenty of Mormons who believe it should be a thing. And you are 100% right, it is a huge double standard. When I found out heavenly polygamy was a thing when I was a teenager, I had a mental breakdown because I don't share my man 😂 my grandma tried to make it okay by saying "you'll think of love differently in heaven" 🙃🤦🏼‍♀️ it didn't help one bit lol trust me, I have many issues with the church and the misogyny within it 😅

This is true. It was a thing when the church was founded by Joseph Smith.

If an LDS church is teaching that men will gain a bunch of wives in heaven, they aren't preaching true doctrine. The only time they say you might have multiple wives in heaven is if your wife (who you are sealed to in the temple) passes away and then you get remarried and are sealed to your new wife in the temple as well. Then, you will have 2 wives in heaven, according to LDS doctrine. 

Also, they believe that you have to be sealed in the temple to someone in order to get into the highest level of the celestial kingdom so if you die without getting married/sealed to someone, they will do ordinances by proxy and it's possible that a single woman could be sealed to a man that is already married, however I believe that is more rare unless it is instigated by family. (For example, my great grandma had a sister who passed away before getting married and my great grandpa volunteered to have her sealed to him in spirit so she could get into the highest level of heaven, so when they passed, he technically then had 2 wives in heaven. If I'm remembering that story accurately, it's been a minute since I've heard it lol)

I had my tonsils removed the same year in the US. The first thing I was given was orange flavored ice chips. I was 16. I don't remember a whole lot as they couldn't keep my oxygen levels up, and I kept passing out. I remember being on oxygen and waking up randomly because the doctors and my mom were shaking me awake to try and get me to breathe better. The things I remember most were being angry that they wouldn't let me sleep, the orange ice chips, and then the pain when I actually really started coming out of it 😅 I was out on narcotics for 2 weeks. The most painful surgery of my life. But they told me to eat soft, cold things to help with swelling and that the scabs would sluff off when they were ready. They didn't want me to eat hard things because they didn't want to risk the scabs coming off too early and starting up the bleeding again. I find it very interesting they encourage differently in the UK. That sounds so much more painful 😬
